correctness.rationale: A fixed barycentric point has constant weights on each rotation orbit of undirected edges, so rescaling orbit weights yields a PL identification with the distance-set simplicial complex. A triangle of selected edge-orbits occurs exactly when signed distances x,y,z in the symmetric step set obey x+y=z modulo n (repeated step values allowed), proving the sum-free equivalence. The assigned verifier enumerates all distance subsets for every integer n=3..21, constructs signed integer boundary matrices and computes exact Smith forms. An independent implementation separately rebuilt all these complexes, confirmed unit nonzero Smith factors for n<=20 and at n=21 factors 1^8 for boundary1 and 1^17,2 for boundary2. The n=21 9-vertex,27-edge,18-facet complex is connected; every edge appears twice and each vertex link is a connected six-cycle. Euler characteristic zero plus the orientation contradiction in the original verifier identifies a nonorientable closed surface, hence the Klein bottle. Torsion computation independently supports the orientation result. The sharpness claim is ONLY the exhausted finite interval, not all larger n.

value.rationale: The first integral torsion threshold in a canonical rotation-fixed graph-property complex is a natural topological cutoff. Exhibiting a nine-vertex Klein bottle as that exact fixed locus reveals a nontrivial torsion transition not predicted by extremal sum-free cardinalities; a finite but full classification up to the threshold is mathematically usable in equivariant graph-complex topology. No claim of a new Klein bottle triangulation is required.

final_claim: For the cyclic-rotation fixed geometric realization of the triangle-free spanning-edge simplicial complex on Z/nZ, all n=3..20 have torsion-free integral homology; the first torsion is at n=21, whose fixed locus has the PL topology of a Klein bottle, f=(9,27,18) and H1=Z plus Z/2.
